name: John Kapantzakis
title: Senior Frontend Engineer
summary: Senior frontend engineer with 12+ years of experience building web products, currently on the React frontend of Netdata Cloud: AI-assisted observability, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration and performance work on data-intensive UIs. Contributor to Hotwire Turbo, co-organiser of SKG JS, the Thessaloniki JavaScript community.

experience.context: Open-source, real-time observability platform. Frontend of Netdata Cloud, a large, data-intensive React application.
bullets: Built frontend capabilities for Netdata's AI assistant, evolving it from a basic chat interface to persistent LLM conversations powered by Netdata-specific tools and investigation workflows. Also implemented frontend support for Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing users to connect external tooling.
Optimized data processing and React rendering to improve performance and eliminate unnecessary remounts.
Cut reported frontend CI runtime by about 60% through Jest test sharding and test-reliability fixes.
Built the foundational Dynamic Configurations UI and continued evolving it to support complex, dynamically generated configuration forms, using the react-jsonschema-form library.

Helped build end-to-end AI Insights investigation reports (generation, rendering, scheduling) and contributed to enterprise identity features: SCIM, SSO, role and room mappings, and label-driven room membership.

experience.context: Job search engine used by 15M+ jobseekers a month across 20 countries.
bullets: Built Labour Market Intelligence, a new data product, from zero to launch in under a year on Next.js, in a team of three (one product manager, two developers).
Built the product's interactive charts and maps with Apache ECharts, visualising hiring demand, salaries and trends across regions.
Shipped search, grouping and filtering by location, sector, salary and other dimensions, so users could explore labour-market data for multiple countries.

experience.context: One of Greece's leading e-commerce marketplaces. Partners department: tooling for merchants.
bullets: Developed and maintained the merchant platform (orders, payments, daily operations) with Ruby on Rails and Hotwire Turbo server rendering, using React for selected views.
Contributed two features to Hotwire Turbo that shipped in Turbo 7 and were credited in the release announcement: the turbo:frame-render event and target elements on fetch events.
Published two articles on the Skroutz engineering blog, on progressive data loading in React and lazy loading with Hotwire.

experience.context: Greek business-software company. Epsilon ESS, an employee self-service web platform on ASP.NET and C#.
bullets: Progressed from junior web designer to full-stack developer responsible for the product's frontend, implementing features end to end from C# backend to TypeScript frontend.
Introduced TypeScript, webpack and Redux-managed asynchronous views into a legacy ASP.NET Web Forms frontend, and added unit tests on both sides (Mocha and Chai, xUnit).
Built a Node.js and Handlebars CLI that generates the boilerplate for a new form: the ASP.NET user control and async handler, the TypeScript page script and Redux state, and the C# data models.
